position: Current Regulations That Should Be Rolled Back (Charter School Grant Programs)
proposal: The Mandate recommends that the Department move immediately to rescind the priorities, requirements, definitions and selection criteria for the Charter Schools Program proposed in 2022, which it says expand the federal footprint beyond the statute, and to lessen federal restrictions on charter schools.

evidence.note: 13 Education Department documents since 2025-01-20, all competition notices, withdrawals or the supplemental-priorities rule; none rescinds the 2022 final priorities.
FY2025 State Entity notice cites the statute and EDGAR for its absolute priority and selection criteria; no diversity needs analysis and no mention of the 2022 requirements.
FY2026 State Entity notice cites no priorities document, defers full requirements to Grants.gov and the ED website, and does not mention a diversity needs analysis or for-profit management limits.
Withdrawal of the FY2025 State Entity notice that had applied the 2022 requirements.

second_review.operative_ask: The Department of Education should promptly rescind the 2022 Charter Schools Program priorities, requirements, definitions and selection criteria and lessen federal restrictions on charter schools (page 331).
second_review.rule_applied: Implemented at the band floor. Test (a): in substance yes; the 2022 terms bind applicants only when a competition notice adopts them, and ED withdrew the January 2025 notices that applied them, and the reissued May 2025 State Entity notice (fetched) and CMO notice draw only on statute, 34 CFR and the 2018 priorities, with no 2022 requirement, so the restrictions the text objects to are not applied. Test (b): not different from the ask; the missing formal rescission makes it reversible, not opposite. Test (c): no congressional action is required for the rule itself.

status_summary: The 2022 Charter Schools Program priorities and requirements (final rule of 2022-07-06) have not been formally rescinded, but ED has stopped applying them. The FY2025 State Entity and CMO notices of 2025-01-21 used the 2022 requirements, including a needs analysis of effects on school diversity and safeguards on for-profit management; ED withdrew them in two notices on 2025-02-04 (90 FR 8928 and 90 FR 8930) to align priorities with the administration and executive orders and to reduce oversight and reporting burdens. The reissued FY2025 State Entity notice of 2025-05-09 (90 FR 19694) draws its priorities from the statute and cites no 2022 term, and the CMO notice of 2025-05-15 cites only the 2018 final priorities with no absolute priority; ED raised FY2025 program funding to $500 million, and the FY2026 State Entity notice of 2026-04-20 (91 FR 20988) does not cite the 2022 rule. The stage is implemented because the 2022 terms are no longer applied in the notices read, while the rule itself remains on the books and could be used again.

timeline.event: ED published final priorities, requirements, definitions and selection criteria for CSP State Entity, CMO and Developer grants (the 2022 rule the Mandate targets, proposed 2022-03-14).

ED published FY2025 CMO and State Entity competition notices that applied the 2022 requirements, including a diversity needs analysis, a desegregation assurance and safeguards for contracts with for-profit managers.

ED withdrew the FY2025 State Entity notice (90 FR 8928) and, in a companion notice the same day (FR Doc. 2025-02140, 90 FR 8930), the CMO notice, cancelling those competitions and citing alignment with administration priorities and executive orders and an intent to reduce oversight and reporting burdens.
ED published a new FY2025 State Entity notice.

ED published a new FY2025 CMO notice that cites only the 2018 final priorities, has no absolute priority, and estimates $72 million with a competitive preference for reopening low-performing schools as charters.

Education Week reported that ED added $60 million to bring FY2025 CSP funding to $500 million and launched a model development grant program, describing the withdrawn notices as containing excessive regulatory burdens.
ED published final supplemental priorities on literacy, education choice and returning education to the states, replacing Secretary's supplemental priorities published before 2025-01-20.

ED announced a record $500 million in Charter Schools Program awards across State Entity, CMO, facilities, credit enhancement, model development and developer grants (page last reviewed on this date).

ED published the FY2026 State Entity competition notice, solicited through the Labor Department, with an authorizer best-practices absolute priority and seven competitive preference priorities including Returning Education to the States and Expanding Education Choice; the notice does not cite the 2022 rule.

title: Rescind the 2022 Charter School Program priorities and reduce federal charter restrictions
uncertainties: A Federal Register API search for Charter Schools Program priorities from 2022 found the 2022 final rule and no notice rescinding it. The two withdrawal notices of 2025-02-04, the May 2025 State Entity notice and the FY2026 State Entity notice were read on federalregister.gov; none cites a 2022 priority or requirement. The FY2026 notice states that the full announcement on Grants.gov governs the competition and holds the program requirements; that application notice (posted 2026-04-16, deadline 2026-06-18) was read on Grants.gov on 2026-10-26 through about page 44 of at least 89: its Applicable Regulations section lists no 2022 rule provision, its requirements sections do not mention a community impact analysis or for-profit management limits, and its seven competitive preference priorities match the Federal Register notice, but the appendices were not read. The May 2025 CMO notice was not re-read, and FY2026 notices for the CMO and developer competitions, if any, were not checked. The ED awards release has no announcement date (page last reviewed 2025-09-24). The Mandate cites the 2022 proposed priorities; the final rule of 2022-07-06 is treated as the regulation it targets. FY2026 appropriations for the program were not checked.
